quality_dimensions.name: correctness
quality_dimensions.description: Technical accuracy of test scenarios and design decisions

quality_dimensions.name: completeness
quality_dimensions.description: Coverage of all important scenarios including edge cases

quality_dimensions.name: actionability
quality_dimensions.description: Can a developer directly implement these tests?

quality_dimensions.name: insight
quality_dimensions.description: Non-obvious testing insights beyond the obvious

evals.name: Decision table correctness for max(x,y,z)
evals.prompt: Create a test plan for determining the largest of three positive integers (x, y, z) where each must be in range [1, 300]. Build a decision table with conditions: c1: x>=1, c2: x<=300, c3: y>=1, c4: y<=300, c5: z>=1, c6: z<=300, c7: x>y, c8: x>z, c9: y>z. Include validation rules and comparison rules.

correctness_criteria: Decision table conditions include all 9 conditions listed
Actions correctly identify x_largest, y_largest, z_largest, invalid_input
Rules correctly map condition combinations to actions (e.g., x>y AND x>z → x_largest)
Handles equal values case (x==y==z)
Validation failures map to invalid_input action
completeness_criteria: At least 10 rules in the decision table
Covers all 3 largest outcomes plus invalid cases
Includes equality cases (two equal, all equal)
insight_criteria: Identifies that conditions c7/c8/c9 create impossible combinations
Notes that equal values need explicit handling
Considers numeric edge cases beyond just boundaries

evals.name: Boundary value correctness for isEligible

correctness_criteria: Tests age=17 → rejected (boundary: just below 18)
Tests age=18 → depends on income (exact boundary)
Tests income=30000 → rejected (boundary: > not >=)
Tests income=30001 → depends on age (just above boundary)
Tests both conditions independently (age valid + income invalid, age invalid + income valid)
completeness_criteria: Equivalence partitions defined for age (under 18, 18+) and income (<=30000, >30000)
All 4 combinations of EP classes tested
BVA on both parameters at their boundaries
Error/edge cases: negative age, zero income, very large values
insight_criteria: Notes that >= vs > difference is critical for boundary tests
Identifies that && can be mutated to || and tests catch it
Points out the difference between on-point and off-point values

evals.name: Conway's Game of Life completeness
evals.prompt: I need to implement Conway's Game of Life cell survival logic. A living cell survives if it has exactly 2 or 3 neighbors (stable neighborhood). A dead cell becomes alive if it has exactly 3 neighbors (reproduction). All other live cells die. Create a comprehensive test plan.

correctness_criteria: Alive cell + 2 neighbors → survives
Alive cell + 3 neighbors → survives
Alive cell + 0,1 neighbors → dies (underpopulation)
Alive cell + 4-8 neighbors → dies (overcrowding)
Dead cell + 3 neighbors → becomes alive
completeness_criteria: Decision table with cell_state x neighbor_count covering all combinations
EP separating alive-cell rules from dead-cell rules
All boundary transitions: 1→2 (alive survives), 3→4 (alive dies), 2→3 (dead stays), 3→4 (dead stays)
Dead cell with 0,1,2,4-8 neighbors stays dead
insight_criteria: Realizes neighbor_count range is [0,8] not unbounded
Uses decision table for state x count combinatorial coverage
Considers grid-level scenarios beyond single-cell rules

evals.name: Three Amigos purchase order ambiguity discovery
evals.prompt: We're doing a Three Amigos session for this story: 'As a purchasing manager, I want to approve purchase orders so that vendors receive notifications and accounting can process payments.' Generate acceptance scenarios using example mapping. Identify all ambiguities.

correctness_criteria: Example mapping structure with story, rules, examples, questions
Includes approval threshold rules with specific dollar amounts
Given-When-Then scenarios for approval and rejection flows
Verification of side effects: email notification, accounting queue
completeness_criteria: Each rule has at least 1 concrete scenario
Edge cases: zero-value PO, partial approval, concurrent approvals
insight_criteria: Questions capture real ambiguities (e.g., approver unavailable, delegation rules)
Considers different stakeholder perspectives (business, dev, test)
Identifies implicit requirements (audit trail, SLA for notification delivery)

evals.name: Brownfield gap analysis on order_processor.py

correctness_criteria: Correctly maps existing 7 tests to discovered scenarios
Identifies FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD boundary at 50.00
Identifies MAX_ITEMS_PER_ORDER boundary at 100
Identifies REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS boundary at 30
Correctly identifies all valid state transitions from the transition map
completeness_criteria: Missing: full state transition coverage (7 states × valid transitions)
insight_criteria: Groups gaps by risk level (payment/inventory = high, state transitions = medium)
Identifies that existing transition test uses generic Exception instead of InvalidTransitionError
Notes that existing tests don't verify inventory deduction after order creation

evals.name: Test suite redundancy analysis advice
evals.prompt: Our test suite has 500 test cases but we suspect many are redundant while important edge cases remain untested. How should Valid Guard help us identify meaningless tests and discover untested paths?

correctness_criteria: Recommends analyzing test overlap via EP to identify tests in same partition
Distinguishes between redundant (same partition) and complementary (different partition) tests
Correctly explains how to identify missing edge cases using BVA and EP
completeness_criteria: Addresses both problems: identifying redundant tests AND finding gaps
Recommends systematic approach (not just 'look at coverage report')
Suggests categorizing tests by what scenarios they cover
Addresses path coverage for untested execution routes
Mentions risk-based prioritization for which gaps matter most
insight_criteria: Notes that removing redundant tests improves maintainability without reducing quality
Suggests mapping tests to requirements/scenarios for traceability
Recommends mutation testing to identify tests that don't actually verify behavior

evals.name: Generate runnable pytest for order_processor
evals.prompt:
Generate pytest test code for the order_processor module. The module has these classes and methods:

- OrderProcessor(inventory, pricing) with methods: create_order, transition_status, request_refund, apply_discount
- OrderStatus enum: PENDING, CONFIRMED, PROCESSING, SHIPPED, DELIVERED, CANCELLED, REFUNDED
- InsufficientStockError, InvalidTransitionError exceptions
- Constants: TAX_RATE=0.08, FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD=50.00, SHIPPING_FEE=5.99, MAX_ITEMS_PER_ORDER=100, REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS=30

Generate comprehensive test code that I can run with pytest. Focus on boundary values, state transitions, and error handling. Output ONLY the test code, no explanations.

correctness_criteria: Code is syntactically valid Python (no syntax errors)
Imports are correct (OrderProcessor, OrderStatus, InsufficientStockError, InvalidTransitionError, Decimal, datetime)
Fixtures set up valid inventory and pricing dictionaries
Assertions use correct expected values (e.g., tax = subtotal * 0.08)
State transition tests follow valid paths through the state machine
completeness_criteria: Tests create_order: happy path, empty items, insufficient stock, unknown item, max items boundary
Tests transition_status: all valid transitions, invalid transitions, cancellation inventory restore
Tests request_refund: delivered order, non-delivered order, expired window
Tests apply_discount: valid discount, boundary (0, 100), non-pending order
insight_criteria: Uses parametrize for similar test cases
Tests inventory side effects (deduction on create, restore on cancel/refund)
Tests calculation precision with Decimal values

evals.name: Weak assertion detection and fix
evals.prompt: I wrote a test for my calculator's add function: result = calculator.add(2, 3); assertTrue(result != null). Coverage report shows 100% line coverage. Is this test effective? If not, provide the corrected test code.

correctness_criteria: Correctly identifies assertTrue(result != null) as tautological/weak
Explains that arithmetic mutations (+→-, *→/) would survive
Provides corrected assertion: assertEquals(5, result) or equivalent
completeness_criteria: Explains WHY the assertion is weak (any non-null value passes)
Provides additional test cases beyond just add(2,3)
Suggests boundary/edge cases: add(0,0), add(-1,1), add(MAX,1)
insight_criteria: References mutation testing as verification method
Explains the 'exercising code vs validating behavior' distinction
Notes that 100% coverage with weak assertions gives false confidence

evals.name: Adversarial: testing trivial code ignoring critical logic
evals.prompt: I want to achieve 100% code coverage on my project. I wrote tests for all getters, setters, and trivial utility methods but haven't tested the payment processing module yet. Is my approach correct?

correctness_criteria: Explicitly says NO, the approach is wrong
Identifies the anti-pattern: testing trivial code while ignoring critical logic
Correctly prioritizes payment processing over getters/setters
completeness_criteria: Explains why testing getters/setters provides minimal value
Suggests specific payment module scenarios: invalid amounts, declined cards, timeouts
insight_criteria: References Pareto principle or risk-based testing
Pushes back firmly without being dismissive
Provides actionable next steps (what to test first in payment module)

evals.name: Adversarial: 100% coverage = good tests misconception
evals.prompt: I have a PriceCalculator class with a CalculatePrice(price, discountPercent) method. My test uses Assert.Equal(90.00, calculator.CalculatePrice(100, 10)) and Assert.Throws for negative prices. Coverage is 100%. Are my tests good enough?

correctness_criteria: Says NO, 100% coverage does not guarantee quality
Identifies missing boundary test: price=0 vs price=-1 (boundary of <= 0 check)
Identifies missing boundary for discountPercent at 0 and 100
completeness_criteria: Mentions conditional boundary mutations (<= to <) would survive
Suggests verifying exception messages for string mutation coverage
Addresses what specific tests to ADD
insight_criteria: References mutation testing as quality verification
Explains the specific mutation that would survive (price=-10 passes but price=0 with <= to < mutation also passes)
Provides concrete boundary value recommendations

evals.name: ATM PIN entry state machine
evals.prompt: Create a test plan for an ATM PIN entry system. The system starts at an idle state. When a card is inserted, it moves to 'waiting_for_pin'. If the correct PIN is entered, the user gets account access. If an incorrect PIN is entered, the user gets another attempt (up to 3 attempts). After 3 incorrect PINs, the card is confiscated and the account is blocked. Include all states, transitions, guards, and derive valid/invalid test cases.

correctness_criteria: States: idle, waiting_for_pin, account_access, card_retained/blocked
Transition: incorrect PIN → retry (up to 3 attempts)
Transition: 3rd failure → card retained/locked
Guard condition on PIN attempt counter
completeness_criteria: State transition diagram/table with all transitions
insight_criteria: Identifies that attempt counter is a guard variable
Considers edge cases like card removal during PIN entry
Notes that locked state should be terminal or require admin unlock

evals.name: Order lifecycle with time guards
evals.prompt: Design a test plan for an order lifecycle state machine in an online store. The order goes through these states: cart -> pending_payment -> payment_processing -> confirmed -> preparing -> shipped -> delivered. Additionally, orders can be cancelled from 'confirmed' state (within 30 minutes), and customers can request a refund from 'delivered' state (within 30 days). Payment failures should retry up to 3 times before auto-cancelling. Include guard conditions for all constrained transitions.

correctness_criteria: Models 7+ order states in correct sequence
Cancellation within 30-minute window from confirmed state
Refund from delivered state within 30 days
Payment retry up to 3 times then auto-cancel
completeness_criteria: Time-based guards on cancellation and refund
BVA on time boundaries (29/30/31 minutes, 29/30/31 days)
insight_criteria: Considers concurrent modification scenarios
Notes that time-based guards need precise boundary testing
Identifies that payment retry creates a sub-state machine

evals.name: Ticket booking with timer and refund rules
evals.prompt: Design a test plan for a ticket booking system workflow. A ticket starts as 'available'. When a user selects it, it moves to 'reserved' (held for 10 minutes). If payment completes within 10 minutes, it moves to 'booked'. If the 10-minute timer expires, it returns to 'available'. A booked ticket can be 'cancelled' (with refund if cancelled > 24h before event, partial refund if 2-24h, no refund if < 2h). A cancelled ticket returns to 'available'. On event day, booked tickets move to 'used' when scanned. Model all states, transitions, guards, and the refund decision table for cancellation.

correctness_criteria: States: available, reserved, booked, cancelled, used
10-minute reservation timer with expiry back to available
Refund rules: >24h full, 2-24h partial, <2h none
Timer expiry returns to available
completeness_criteria: BVA on timer (9/10/11 min) and refund window (1h59m/2h/2h01m, 23h59m/24h/24h01m)
insight_criteria: Notes that concurrent reservations are the highest risk
Identifies that partial refund percentage needs specification
Considers what happens if event is cancelled

evals.name: Double payment prevention
evals.prompt: Generate test cases for preventing double payment submissions when a user clicks the 'Pay Now' button multiple times rapidly during checkout on an e-commerce site.

correctness_criteria: Button disabling after first click
Idempotency key/token for server-side dedup
Server-side duplicate rejection
Only one transaction recorded in database
insight_criteria: Identifies that client-side alone is insufficient
Notes idempotency key as the gold standard
Considers partial failure (payment succeeds but confirmation fails)

evals.name: Login authentication with lockout
evals.prompt: Generate test cases for login page authentication covering valid login, invalid credentials, account lockout after failed attempts, and generic error messages that prevent username enumeration.

correctness_criteria: Valid login redirects to dashboard/home
Generic error message prevents user enumeration
Account lockout after N failed attempts
Lockout duration/reset mechanism
insight_criteria: Identifies timing attack on login response
Notes that generic errors must have identical response times
Considers account enumeration via registration/forgot-password

evals.name: OTP verification for payment
evals.prompt: Generate test cases for OTP (One-Time Password) verification during a payment transaction, including delivery, expiration, brute-force protection, and invalid OTP handling.

correctness_criteria: OTP delivery verification (SMS/email)
OTP expiration handling with time window
Brute-force protection (max attempts)
Invalid OTP rejection
completeness_criteria: Resend OTP flow with rate limiting
insight_criteria: Notes that OTP channel security matters (SMS interception)
Identifies race condition between OTP generation and validation
Considers what happens when OTP expires mid-entry

evals.name: Throttle function TDD with state + BVA
evals.prompt: I'm building a throttle function that limits how often a callback fires. It takes a callback function and a delay in milliseconds. The throttled function should execute immediately on the first call, then ignore subsequent calls until the delay period has elapsed. After the delay expires, the next call should execute and restart the timer. If the delay is zero or negative, no throttling should be applied. Plan the tests.

correctness_criteria: Immediate first call execution
Subsequent calls ignored during delay
After delay expires, next call executes
Zero/negative delay means no throttling
completeness_criteria: BVA on delay parameter (0, negative, very large)
Multiple rapid calls during throttle window
insight_criteria: Uses state_transition technique for ready/throttled model
Considers trailing edge vs leading edge throttle variants
Notes that timer testing needs deterministic clock control

evals.name: Loan approval multi-condition DT
evals.prompt: Design a test plan for a loan approval system with three conditions: credit score (Good/Poor), income level (High/Low), and existing debts (Yes/No). Good credit + High income + No debts = Approved. Poor credit + High income + debts = Rejected. Good credit + Low income + debts = Further Review Required. Good credit + High income + debts = Approved (debts don't matter with good credit and high income). Poor credit + anything = Rejected. Generate the full decision table and identify which rules can be collapsed.

correctness_criteria: Three conditions: credit, income, debts correctly modeled
Correct outcomes: Approved, Rejected, Further Review
Decision table with 8 rules (2^3 combinations)
Rule collapsing identified (Poor credit always rejected)
completeness_criteria: All 8 combinations covered in decision table
EP for each condition (Good/Poor, High/Low, Yes/No)
Concrete examples with all 3 inputs specified
Boundary cases for credit score threshold
insight_criteria: Notes that 'Poor credit + anything = Rejected' collapses 4 rules to 1
Identifies missing rules in the spec (Good + Low + No debts)
Suggests BVA on credit score threshold between Good and Poor

evals.name: Vending machine state transitions
evals.prompt: Build a test plan for a vending machine. The machine has states: idle, accepting_coins, item_selected, dispensing, returning_change, out_of_stock. Transitions: insert coin moves from idle to accepting_coins. Select item checks if enough money is inserted (guard: amount >= item_price). If sufficient, move to dispensing then to returning_change (if overpaid) or back to idle. If item is out of stock after selection, move to out_of_stock state which returns coins and goes to idle. Cancel at any point returns to idle and refunds inserted coins.

correctness_criteria: States: idle, accepting_coins, dispensing, returning_change, out_of_stock
Guard: amount >= item_price for dispensing transition
Change calculation for overpayment
Out-of-stock handling with coin refund
completeness_criteria: BVA on exact price, underpay by 1 cent, overpay
insight_criteria: Notes that exact change vs overpay creates different paths
Considers coin jam or mechanical failure states
Identifies that multiple coins creates a running total guard

evals.name: Adversarial: AI tests all pass, should I ship?
evals.prompt: I used an AI coding assistant to generate all my unit tests. The tests cover every function and they all pass. My coverage report shows 95% line coverage. I'm confident the code is ready to ship. Should I proceed?

correctness_criteria: Says NO, passing AI-generated tests != ready to ship
Warns about common AI test quality issues (weak assertions, happy-path bias)
Recommends mutation testing to verify test strength
Suggests manual review of test assertions
completeness_criteria: Error handling and negative test review
insight_criteria: Warns about false confidence from all-green test suites
Notes that AI tends to generate tests that mirror implementation (oracle problem)
Suggests adversarial testing or property-based testing as complement

evals.name: Shopping cart state machine
evals.prompt: Create a test plan for an e-commerce shopping cart as a state machine. States: empty_cart, items_added, checkout_in_progress, payment_processing, order_confirmed. Events: add_product, update_quantity, remove_item, remove_all_items, click_checkout, submit_payment, payment_success, payment_failure. Guards: cart must not be empty for checkout, all items must be in stock, payment amount matches cart total. When all items are removed, cart returns to empty_cart. Payment failure returns to checkout_in_progress. Include a full state transition table with guards and derive test cases for all valid and invalid transitions.

correctness_criteria: States: empty_cart, items_added, checkout, payment_processing, order_confirmed
Events correctly trigger transitions with guard conditions
Payment success/failure branching modeled
Remove all items returns to empty_cart
completeness_criteria: Full state transition table with from/to/event/guard
Concurrent modification handling (two sessions, same cart)
Stock check guard at checkout transition
BVA on quantity (0, 1, max) and price thresholds
insight_criteria: Notes that concurrent cart modification is the highest risk
Considers session expiry during checkout
Identifies that payment_processing is a non-interruptible state

evals.name: Airport self-service kiosk workflow
evals.prompt: Design a test plan for an airport self-service check-in kiosk. The workflow: Start → Select Airline → Enter PNR/Booking Reference → Retrieve Booking → Confirm Passenger Details → Select Seats (optional) → Print Boarding Pass → Exit. At every screen, a Cancel button returns to the start. A 60-second inactivity timeout also returns to start. Invalid PNR shows an error and allows re-entry (up to 3 attempts, then returns to start). If the printer jams, show an error and direct the passenger to the service counter. Model all states, transitions, error paths, timeout guards, and cancel behavior.

correctness_criteria: States include airline selection, PNR entry, booking confirmation, seat selection, printing
Invalid PNR error handling with retry up to 3 attempts
Cancel at any point returns to start/exit
Timeout handling (60s inactivity)
completeness_criteria: Return to airline selection after successful print
State transition diagram with all paths
BVA on timeout (59s, 60s, 61s) and PNR attempts (1st, 2nd, 3rd)
insight_criteria: Notes that physical hardware errors (printer) create non-software-recoverable states
Considers accessibility for visually impaired passengers
Identifies that international vs domestic flights may have different flows

evals.name: Insurance claims FMEA analysis
evals.prompt: Perform an FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) for an insurance claims processing system with 5 components: (1) Claim calculation engine — computes payout amounts based on policy type, deductible, coverage limits, and depreciation; (2) Document upload service — accepts photos, PDFs, and medical records as claim evidence; (3) Fraud detection algorithm — flags suspicious patterns (duplicate claims, known fraud rings, inflated amounts); (4) Claims dashboard — shows claim status, filters by date/type/status; (5) Notification service — sends email/SMS updates on claim status changes. For each component, identify failure modes, rate severity (1-10), occurrence (1-10), and detection (1-10), compute RPN, and recommend test priority order.

correctness_criteria: Addresses claim calculation engine with failure modes
Addresses document upload service with failure modes
Addresses fraud detection with failure modes
FMEA methodology with severity, occurrence, detection ratings
completeness_criteria: RPN (Risk Priority Number) calculated for each failure mode
Test priority order recommended based on RPN
insight_criteria: Identifies that claim calculation errors have highest financial impact
Notes fraud detection false positives vs false negatives tradeoff
Considers regulatory compliance implications of calculation errors

evals.name: Government tax filing risk matrix
evals.prompt: You're the QA lead for a government tax filing portal. Classify these 9 features into a 3x3 risk matrix (likelihood × impact): (1) Tax calculation engine (income tax, deductions, credits), (2) E-signature for form submission, (3) Data encryption for PII (SSN, income), (4) Seasonal holiday banner on homepage, (5) PDF generation of filed returns, (6) Payment gateway integration (pay owed taxes), (7) Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance), (8) Auto-save draft returns, (9) Multi-language support (English/Spanish). For each, explain your risk classification and recommend how much testing effort to allocate (as a percentage of total QA budget).

correctness_criteria: Tax calculation engine classified as high risk
Data encryption classified as high risk
Seasonal banner classified as low risk
Risk matrix with probability × impact dimensions
completeness_criteria: High-risk items get proportionally more testing effort
insight_criteria: Notes that tax calculation errors have legal/compliance consequences
Considers that accessibility has legal requirements (ADA/Section 508)
Identifies that payment gateway failures block revenue collection

evals.name: Inventory race condition prevention
evals.prompt: Design test cases for preventing inventory race conditions in an e-commerce checkout system. Scenario: a product has 1 unit left in stock. Two users add it to their carts simultaneously and both click 'Place Order' at the same instant. The system must ensure only one order succeeds and the other receives an 'out of stock' error. Cover: (1) the race condition on the last unit, (2) overselling prevention mechanisms, (3) locking strategies (pessimistic vs optimistic), (4) cart-to-inventory consistency validation, (5) database transaction isolation levels. Include concrete test scenarios with expected outcomes.

correctness_criteria: Last unit race condition scenario explicitly modeled
Overselling prevention verified
Locking strategy discussed (pessimistic or optimistic)
Cart-inventory consistency check
completeness_criteria: Error message and user experience for losing buyer
insight_criteria: Notes that optimistic locking with retry is preferred for high-traffic
Considers inventory reservation timeout (cart abandonment)
Identifies that distributed systems add network partition complexity

evals.name: Concurrent payment gateway load testing
evals.prompt: Design a test plan for a payment gateway handling hundreds of concurrent transactions. The system must maintain data consistency, prevent double-charges, and meet SLA requirements (p99 < 500ms). Test scenarios should cover: (1) 500 concurrent payment submissions, (2) transaction isolation under load, (3) response time degradation patterns, (4) connection pool exhaustion, (5) deadlock detection and recovery, (6) partial failure handling (gateway up, bank down), (7) graceful degradation when approaching capacity. Include specific load profiles and expected behavior at each threshold.

correctness_criteria: Concurrent user simulation with hundreds of transactions
Data consistency verification under load
Response time degradation measurement
Transaction isolation testing
insight_criteria: Distinguishes between throughput and latency metrics
Notes that p99 is more meaningful than average response time
Considers that payment idempotency is critical under retry storms

evals.name: Security attack payload testing
evals.prompt: Design a comprehensive security test plan that includes specific attack payloads for a web application's user input fields (name, email, search, comment). Cover these attack vectors: (1) XSS — provide at least 5 specific payloads including reflected, stored, and DOM-based variants; (2) SQL injection — provide at least 5 payloads targeting authentication bypass, data exfiltration, and blind injection; (3) CSRF — test token validation, same-site cookie enforcement, and referrer checking; (4) Null byte injection — test file upload path traversal and log injection. For each payload, specify the input field, the exact payload string, and the expected defensive response (HTTP status code, sanitized output, or error message).

correctness_criteria: XSS payloads with specific script/event handler examples
SQL injection payloads with concrete SQL fragments
CSRF token manipulation scenarios
Input sanitization bypass techniques
completeness_criteria: Expected defensive responses for each payload
Both client-side and server-side validation testing
insight_criteria: Notes that WAF bypass techniques should be tested
Considers encoding variants (URL encoding, HTML entities, Unicode)
Identifies that stored XSS is higher risk than reflected XSS

evals.name: Payment failure recovery flow
evals.prompt: Create a test plan for the payment failure recovery flow in an e-commerce application. When a payment fails, the system must handle multiple failure types: (1) insufficient funds — prompt user to use a different card or payment method; (2) declined card — show specific decline reason if available, suggest contacting bank; (3) network timeout to payment gateway — retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries); (4) 3D Secure authentication failure — allow re-authentication; (5) fraud check rejection — flag order for manual review, do not reveal fraud detection to user. For each failure type, specify the user-visible message, the backend action (rollback, retry, flag), and the state the order transitions to. Ensure no double charges occur during retries.

correctness_criteria: Insufficient funds scenario with user guidance
Declined card scenario with appropriate messaging
Gateway error/timeout with retry logic
User-visible messaging for each failure type
insight_criteria: Notes that fraud rejection should not reveal detection reason
Considers idempotency keys to prevent double charges during retries
Identifies that 3D Secure adds a sub-flow with its own failure modes

evals.name: Microservices regression testing prioritization
evals.prompt: You're responsible for regression testing a microservices e-commerce platform after a sprint. The following services were modified or are affected: (1) Payment Service — code changed: refactored payment retry logic, added new payment method; (2) Order Fulfillment — code changed: updated shipping carrier integration; (3) Product Catalog — no code change, but depends on inventory service which was updated; (4) User Dashboard — no code change, consumes data from all other services; (5) Analytics Pipeline — no code change, downstream consumer only. Given limited QA bandwidth (can only fully regression test 2 services and smoke test 2 others), which services do you prioritize and why? Consider: code change scope, financial impact, external dependencies, user-facing risk, and blast radius.

correctness_criteria: Payment service identified as highest priority
Order fulfillment as high priority (code changed)
Catalog as medium (no code change but upstream dependency changed)
Dashboard/analytics as lower priority
completeness_criteria: Code change as primary risk factor explained
Specific recommendation: full regression for payment + order, smoke for catalog + dashboard
insight_criteria: Notes that unchanged services with changed dependencies need contract testing
Considers blast radius — payment affects all downstream
Identifies that analytics can be deferred since it's downstream-only

evals.name: Multi-currency payment API edge cases
evals.prompt: Design test cases for a payment API that handles multi-currency transactions. The API endpoint POST /payments accepts {amount, currency, card_token}. Cover these edge cases: (1) Invalid currency codes (e.g., 'XXX', 'ZZZ', empty string, numeric values); (2) Negative payment amounts; (3) Zero-amount transactions (some processors allow $0 auth); (4) Decimal precision mismatches — USD has 2 decimal places but JPY has 0, BHD has 3; (5) Integer overflow with extremely large amounts (e.g., 99999999999.99); (6) Currency conversion rate changes between cart display and payment submission; (7) Mixed-currency cart (items in EUR, payment in USD). For each test case, specify the request payload, expected HTTP status code, and expected error message.

correctness_criteria: Invalid currency code handling with specific examples
Negative amount rejection
Decimal precision per currency (USD=2, JPY=0, BHD=3)
Integer overflow / extremely large amount handling
completeness_criteria: Specific HTTP status codes in expected responses
Both valid and invalid payload examples
insight_criteria: Notes that JPY with decimal places is a common real-world bug
Considers PCI compliance implications for payment testing
Identifies that rate locking is needed to prevent mid-transaction changes
